points.quote: To support academic integrity, GenAI can only be used by students in ways that are approved in advance by their lecturer.
points.anchor: Principles Underpinning use of AI and GenAI in TU Dublin
points.gist: Students can only use GenAI in ways their lecturer has approved in advance.

points.quote: Level 1: No Artificial Intelligence (AI). The assessment must be completed entirely without AI assistance. AI must not be used at any point during the assessment.
points.anchor: Use of Artificial Intelligence Assessment Scale (AIAS)
points.gist: At Level 1 of the AI Assessment Scale, assessments must be completed entirely without AI at any point.

points.quote: Level 3: AI-Assisted Editing. AI can be used to make improvements to the clarity or quality of student-created work to improve the final output, but no new content can be created using AI.
points.anchor: Use of Artificial Intelligence Assessment Scale (AIAS)
points.gist: At Level 3, AI may improve clarity or quality of student-created work, but may not create new content.

points.quote: Level 4: AI Task Completion, Human Evaluation. AI is used to complete certain elements of the task, with students providing discussion or commentary on the AI generated content.
points.anchor: Use of Artificial Intelligence Assessment Scale (AIAS)
points.gist: At Level 4, AI completes certain task elements and students discuss or comment on the AI-generated content.

points.quote: Level 5: Full AI. AI should be used as a 'co-pilot' in order to meet the requirements of the assessment, allowing for a collaborative approach with AI and enhancing creativity.
points.anchor: Use of Artificial Intelligence Assessment Scale (AIAS)
points.gist: At Level 5, AI is used as a co-pilot to meet the assessment requirements.

points.quote: Failure to adhere to these guidelines or the inappropriate use of AI, as determined by the relevant Faculty, may result in disciplinary action as it is a breach of academic integrity.
points.anchor: Principles Underpinning use of AI and GenAI in TU Dublin
points.gist: Failing to follow the guidelines or using AI inappropriately, as the Faculty determines, may lead to disciplinary action for breach of academic integrity.

points.quote: Students accept that they are wholly responsible for ensuring the veracity, accuracy and/or creative merit of the output generated by any artificial intelligence model.
points.anchor: Principles Underpinning use of AI and GenAI in TU Dublin
points.gist: Students are wholly responsible for the veracity, accuracy and creative merit of any AI model output.

points.quote: The details of how GenAI has been used in an assessment should be presented in line with the assessment guidelines, e.g. citations, supply of prompts used
points.anchor: Table 1: Ethical Principles on the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
points.gist: Details of GenAI use in an assessment should follow assessment guidelines, for example citations or supplying the prompts used.

points.quote: Personal data should not be entered into GenAI systems that are not supported/approved by the University.
points.anchor: Table 1: Ethical Principles on the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
points.gist: Personal data should not be entered into GenAI systems that the University has not supported or approved.

points.quote: This includes the use of any system that amends text beyond simple spelling and grammar checks.
points.anchor: Principles Underpinning use of AI and GenAI in TU Dublin
points.gist: Recording of GenAI use covers any system that amends text beyond simple spelling and grammar checks.

points.quote: For citation and referencing guidelines, please consult the relevant Faculty and the AI Guidance Note available in the Referencing LibGuides from Library Services.
points.anchor: Principles Underpinning use of AI and GenAI in TU Dublin
points.gist: For citation and referencing guidelines, consult the Faculty and the AI Guidance Note in the Referencing LibGuides from Library Services.

points.quote: In group assessment, an ‘accountability agreement’ might be used to ensure everyone agrees to abide by the same standards.
points.anchor: Table 1: Ethical Principles on the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
points.gist: In group assessment, an accountability agreement might be used so everyone agrees to the same standards.

points.quote: Students should actively consider the potential for a particular GenAI tool to be exclusionary or biased and call out such outputs when possible
points.anchor: Table 1: Ethical Principles on the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
points.gist: Students should consider whether a GenAI tool may be exclusionary or biased and call out such outputs when possible.

points.quote: GenAI should not be solely used to make decisions about the quality of a student, although it may be used supportively.
points.anchor: Table 1: Ethical Principles on the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
points.gist: GenAI should not be solely used to make decisions about the quality of a student, though it may be used supportively.
